svg.title: A nurse obtains a pulse oximetry reading of 84% on a client who is alert, conversing in full sentences, and has pink mucous membranes and unlabored respirations. Which of the following factors could account for an inaccurate reading? (Select all that apply.)
svg.desc: PULSE OXIMETRY REQUIRES ADEQUATE ARTERIAL PULSATILE BLOOD FLOW AND AN UNOBSTRUCTED LIGHT PATH, so dark nail polish, peripheral vasoconstriction from cold, motion such as shivering, and hypotension with poor perfusion all produce falsely low or unreliable readings. The earlobe is an acceptable alternate sensor site and does not cause error, and a low-grade fever does not invalidate the reading. When the reading does not match the clinical picture, the nurse assesses the client first and then corrects the technical problem.
